definitions.explanation: the aesthetic quality of blur in out-of-focus areas of a photograph, now used internationally as a photography term
in Japanese comedy (especially manzai), the person who makes absurd statements or acts silly, contrasted with the tsukkomi

examples.japanese: ボケの{美|うつく}しい{写真|しゃしん}が{撮|と}れた。
examples.english: I took a photo with beautiful bokeh.

examples.japanese: {背景|はいけい}ボケを{活|い}かした{撮影|さつえい}をする。
このレンズはボケが{綺麗|きれい}だ。
ボケとツッコミの{掛|か}け{合|あ}いが{面白|おもしろ}い。
examples.english: The back-and-forth between the funny man and straight man is amusing.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{漫才|まんざい}でボケ{担当|たんとう}だ。
examples.english: He plays the funny man role in manzai.

examples.japanese: ボケ{防止|ぼうし}のために{脳|のう}トレをしている。
examples.english: I'm doing brain training to prevent senility.

examples.japanese: {年|とし}をとってボケてきた。
examples.english: As I got older, I've become forgetful.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}のボケが{進|すす}んでいる。

notes:
PHOTOGRAPHY (SENSE 1):
'Bokeh' has been adopted into English as a photography term. It refers to the quality of the out-of-focus areas in an image.
- {背景|はいけい}ボケ - background blur
- {玉|たま}ボケ - circular bokeh balls (from point light sources)
- {前|まえ}ボケ - foreground blur

COMEDY (SENSE 2):
In manzai comedy, the ボケ makes absurd statements or acts foolish, while the ツッコミ (straight man) corrects or retorts.
- ボケ{担当|たんとう} - the funny man role
- ボケを{入|い}れる - to insert a joke

AGING (SENSE 3):
Used to describe age-related cognitive decline. Can be considered somewhat casual or even insensitive depending on context.
- ボケ{防止|ぼうし} - prevention of senility
- {認知症|にんちしょう} - dementia (medical term)
